entries.complaint: The glossary entry for 'static pressure (fire flow)' says not to render it as 'a zero-flow or no-demand pressure' because that reading is 'always a higher number than this column reports', but it never states what the column DOES report instead (presumably the pressure at the junction under its normal baseline demand, before the fire-flow test load is added, rather than a true hydrostatic zero-everywhere pressure). I translated it with the literal, established engineering term 'Statischer Druck' rather than a German equivalent of 'rest pressure' (which CLAUDE.md records as a struck substitution for the same reason in English), but I could not confirm from the payload alone that this is the exact physical quantity meant.
readings: Statischer Druck (the standard German fire-flow-testing term, literal cognate of the English) (chosen)
A paraphrase naming 'pressure under normal demand, before the test flow', which is more precise but abandons the established short professional term

entries.complaint: The 'fire flow' term family (fire flow / required fire flow / available fire flow) has three separate glossary entries, all marked '[needs translation sprint]' with no preferred_translation. This whole Fire Flow feature is new to the German file, so there is no incumbent rendering anywhere else in lib/lang.ec.de.php to check consistency against. I coined 'Löschwasserbedarf' for the required quantity (this is genuinely the standard German water-utility term for a required fire-fighting flow rate, e.g. DVGW W405) and 'Löschwassermenge' for the general/available quantity, but since no other language file or prior sprint established this, a native German water-utility reviewer should confirm the choice before it becomes the incumbent for future sprints.
readings: Löschwasserbedarf (required) / Löschwassermenge (general, available) — matches DVGW terminology (chosen)
A more literal calque such as 'erforderlicher Brandschutzdurchfluss', which is not idiomatic German water-utility usage

entries.complaint: This button's English label is 'Run', while the pre-existing lpn_time_run key (a different button, in the Time panel) is labelled 'Calculate' and is already translated 'Berechnen'. It is not stated whether the two English words were chosen to name the SAME action in two places or deliberately different ones (the fire-flow run tests many junctions in a loop, the time run advances the clock). I translated lpn_ff_calculate as 'Starten' to keep it distinct from the established 'Berechnen', but if 'Run' and 'Calculate' were meant to read as synonyms throughout the suite, 'Starten' breaks that parallel.
readings: Starten, to keep it visibly distinct from the Time panel's Berechnen button (chosen)
Berechnen, treating 'Run' and 'Calculate' as the same concept across both panels
